entities.summary: Kenneth Tompkins Bainbridge was an American physicist at Harvard University who worked on cyclotron research. His accurate measurements of mass differences between nuclear isotopes allowed him to confirm Albert Einstein's mass–energy equivalence concept. He was the Director of the Manhattan Project's Trinity nuclear test, which took place July 16, 1945. Bainbridge described the Trinity explosion as a "foul and awesome display". He remarked to J. Robert Oppenheimer immediately after the test, "Now we are all sons of bitches." This marked the beginning of his dedication to ending the testing of nuclear weapons and to efforts to maintain civilian control of future developments in that field.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bainbridge's accurate measurements of mass differences between nuclear isotopes confirmed Einstein's mass–energy equivalence concept, a crucial step towards understanding nuclear reactions. His leadership in the Manhattan Project and subsequent advocacy for civilian control of nuclear weapons had far-reaching consequences for global security and international relations.
